transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Ever since a friend from my choir passed away so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I cry over little things like the potluck lists, and calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. I’ve even missed church planning things I never would’ve missed before.
Are these feelings mostly about your friend who died?

Yes, I think it started with her passing. Ever since then, little things like the potluck lists make me cry, and phone calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. I’ve even been missing church planning things I normally wouldn’t miss.
Have you been worrying a lot about many different parts of your life, not just your friend’s death?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s about lots of different things. It mostly seems tied to losing her and how that’s affected everything.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day nearly every day?
I’m not sure it’s most of the day, every day. I do get sad, especially when something reminds me of her, but it seems to come and go.
Since your friend died, have you been feeling especially anxious or on edge?
Yes. Since she died, I get worked up over things that never used to bother me, like phone calls. I just don’t feel like myself.
Did these symptoms start within three months after your friend passed away?
Yes. She died about a month ago, and I started falling apart with the church planning after that happened.
Has this been making it hard for you to carry out your usual responsibilities?
Yes. I’ve had to let other people at church take over the phone calls, the lists, and parts of the luncheon. I’m just not keeping up the way I always did before.
Since your friend died, have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not sure I’ve noticed that exactly.
Since your friend died, have you noticed a change in your appetite?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed any change in my appetite.
Since your friend died, have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear change in my sleep.
Since your friend died, have you been feeling down or hopeless?
Yes... since she died, I’ve been feeling pretty down. I cry over little things, like the potluck lists, and things I used to manage easily can get me all worked up.
Since your friend died, have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living or thoughts of harming yourself?
No, I haven’t had thoughts like that.
Since your friend died, have you been having trouble concentrating?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular problem concentrating.
Since your friend died, have you been feeling both anxious and sad?
Yes, both. I’ve been sad and crying easily, and I get all worked up over things I used to handle without much trouble.
Do you feel your reaction to your friend’s death has been stronger than what you would normally expect for yourself?

Yes, I do. Ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. I’ll cry over something small like the potluck lists, and calls I used to handle easily get me all worked up. I’ve even missed church planning things I never would have missed before.
